original_test_intent: Verify the SMBIOS Type 4 Max Speed metadata for every expected processor record matches the approved firmware-reported maximum speed in MHz or supported unknown value, is internally consistent with Current Speed where both are valid, and persists after reboot without claiming runtime boost performance.
original_method: Capture all raw/decoded Type 4 records, bind by socket/status, compare the raw 16-bit Max Speed and decoded MHz to the approved per-CPU metadata baseline, check declared Current Speed does not exceed a valid declared maximum unless the project documents different semantics, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the per-socket metadata baseline, unknown/consistency policy and reboot plan. Collection and comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Approved Max Speed MHz or zero/unknown policy per expected processor record
Definition of firmware-declared Max Speed versus base/turbo/runtime frequency
Max Speed versus Current Speed consistency rule
Expected socket/population and CPU model mapping
Validated raw/decoded tooling and approved reboot/OOB plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS/CPU inventory only; do not change governors, turbo, power limits, clocks or firmware.
Preserve raw 16-bit values, decoded MHz, all Type 4 records and errors; a grep list is incomplete evidence.
Do not substitute a transient OS frequency sample or benchmark result for this declared SMBIOS field.
Do not reject zero/unknown without approved applicability, and compare Max/Current only when both encodings are valid under the project policy.
Stop on invalid units, missing/duplicate records, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete Type 4 records, bind sockets/status, compare raw/decoded Max Speed and approved internal consistency before/after reboot.
Do not tune performance, assert runtime frequency coverage or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve expected Max Speed, zero/unknown handling and advertised-versus-runtime meaning.
Resolve firmware metadata versus CPU product specification differences and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is correct, but grep loses socket/raw context, suppresses errors and cannot prove complete inventory, unknown handling or Max/Current consistency.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive full decoded/raw Type 4 data with tool/errors, bind records by socket/status and retain Max Speed alongside Current Speed and CPU identity for scoped consistency checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Max Speed scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Retain raw and decoded MHz per socket, apply the approved zero/unknown rule, compare to the platform's declared SMBIOS baseline and evaluate only defined Max/Current internal consistency without runtime stress or tuning.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, parser/dmidecode, BIOS, CPU and platform-recipe revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Max Speed/Current Speed semantics, approved processor/platform recipe and installed tooling documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds raw units, complete per-socket mapping, unknown handling and bounded internal consistency while rejecting silent runtime-frequency substitution.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; runtime frequency/boost behavior remains separate coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware-reported maximum may represent a configured or nominal value and is not proof that workloads reach a particular boost clock.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve zero/unknown or a platform-specific declared maximum distinct from vendor turbo marketing, but must document the per-socket semantics and retain raw values.
expected_evidence: Approval, expected per-socket Max Speed/unknown/consistency policy and tool/SMBIOS versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 table with raw/decoded Max and correlated Current Speed
Engineer verdict and separate runtime-frequency reference if required

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and criterion coherently target Type 4 Max Speed metadata; runtime performance is not requested by the source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The field is safely readable; expected value and semantic policy are readiness inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds complete records, raw MHz, unknown policy and internal consistency.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps advertised-versus-runtime separation while correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adds scoped Max/Current consistency without converting the case into a performance test.

review_improvement: Prevents one displayed MHz value from hiding missing sockets, wrong units or impossible metadata and avoids false claims about runtime boost behavior.
independent_technical_reasoning: Once the declared baseline and semantics are approved, the core collection/comparison/reboot flow is entirely software-controlled.
